summary: Strong T1 for monlist/mode6/peer_list (deterministic-on-vuln), plus a solid T0 CVE-version gate covering 6 CVEs across 4.2.6-4.2.8p14. Nothing sends destructive spoofed packets to prove CVE-2020-11868 off-path desync or CVE-2015-7871 crypto-NAK — those stay banner-based T0. The most impactful promotion is turning the monlist client list into a shared_users/known_hosts feed for the rest of the engagement.

findings.title_pattern: NTP monlist enabled (CVE-2013-5211) — amplification + client disclosure
findings.tier_evidence: Only a vulnerable ntpd answers REQ_MON_GETLIST_1 with payload bytes; recce counts and parses client IPs.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-ingest disclosed client IPs into the known_hosts shared surface for cross-service pivoting. For amplification proof, measure BAF explicitly in a report chart; consider optional --amp-probe that measures response size vs multiple request sizes (still low risk).
findings.tester_next_step: ntpdc -n -c monlist <ip>  # ingest client list, then nxc smb <clients> -u '' -p '' to catch null-session hosts among them.

findings.title_pattern: NTP mode-6 control queries allowed (version / OS disclosure)
findings.tier_evidence: Only ntpd with restrict-noquery not set returns readvar; parses system vars.
findings.promotion_notes: Add CVE-2020-11868 amplification probe (mode-6 REQ_READVAR spoofed to a canary — measurable BAF) as gated PoC; also consume the OS/kernel/processor strings into a shared_os_fingerprints surface consumed by exploit-selection.
findings.tester_next_step: ntpq -c readvar <ip>; ntpq -c 'as' <ip>; for CVE-2020-11868 amp check use nmap --script ntp-monlist or hping3 --udp -p 123 --spoof <victim> -d 12.

findings.tier_evidence: Version-based CVE gate — not exploitation evidence (vendor backports possible).
findings.promotion_notes: Add active PoCs for the highest-impact CVEs: CVE-2014-9295 (autokey) reachability probe (send crypto packet, observe crash/decline non-destructively), CVE-2015-7871 crypto-NAK bypass test. High risk = potential DoS/desync on target ntpd.
findings.tester_next_step: ntpq -c readvar <ip>; searchsploit ntpd <ver>; for CVE-2014-9295 test with: python3 -c 'from scapy.all import *; send(IP(dst="<ip>")/UDP(sport=123,dport=123)/Raw(load=b"\x17\x00\x00\x02\x00\x00\x00\x00..."))'.

findings.title_pattern: NTP peer list readable (internal time topology)
findings.tier_evidence: REQ_PEER_LIST returns payload only when mode-7 accessible and peers configured.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-ingest peer IPs into the known_gateways/known_hosts shared surface — an upstream NTP peer on corp LAN is almost always a DC or appliance.
findings.tester_next_step: ntpq -p <ip>; enqueue each peer for full port sweep (nmap -Pn -sS -p- <peer>) — DCs and appliances almost always come up.

findings.title_pattern: Host clock skew exceeds the Kerberos tolerance
findings.tier_evidence: Skew computed from actual client-server round-trip midpoint — deterministic measurement.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-adjust the scanner's own local clock (via faketime wrapper or ntpdate-under-container) before running kerbrute/GetNPUsers so Kerberos operations don't fail from skew after this warning fires.
findings.tester_next_step: sudo ntpdate -u <ip>; then re-run: GetNPUsers.py -no-pass -usersfile users.txt <domain>/@<dc> and confirm KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW is gone.
